# Tulyro — Full Tool Reference (llms-full.txt)

> Tulyro is a collection of free browser-only tools. No signup. No watermark. Nothing you enter
> is sent to a server — every calculation, conversion, and export happens in the visitor's
> browser. Results are informational estimates, not professional advice. This file is the
> machine-readable companion to https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/llms.txt

## Entity facts

- Name: Tulyro
- Website: https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/
- Contact: Tulyrotools@gmail.com
- Model: free browser-only tools; no accounts, no backend, no database, no watermark, no popups.
- Technology: static site. No cookies are set by the tools themselves. Text to speech uses voices
  provided by the visitor's own browser.
- What Tulyro does not do: it does not store input, does not require accounts, does not add
  watermarks, and does not present invented statistics, reviews, or ratings.

## Tools

### Age Calculator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/calculators/age-calculator/

An age calculator finds the exact time between a date of birth and a chosen date, expressed as
completed years, remaining months, and remaining days. Inputs: a date of birth (1 January 1900
through today; future dates are rejected with a plain-language message). Outputs: exact age in
years/months/days, total calendar days lived, and the next birthday with a countdown. Method:
the calculator advances the birth date month by month on the local calendar instead of dividing
by 365.25, so months of different lengths and leap years are handled correctly. A 29 February
birthday is treated as 1 March in a non-leap year.

### EMI Calculator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/calculators/emi-calculator/

An EMI is a fixed monthly payment that repays a loan over a set tenure, with each payment
covering that month's interest plus part of the principal. This page is written for Indian
readers and formats results in rupees with Indian digit grouping. Inputs: loan amount, annual
interest rate, and tenure in years or months. Outputs: monthly EMI, total payment, and total
interest. Formula (reducing balance): EMI = P × r × (1+r)^n ÷ ((1+r)^n − 1), where P is the
loan amount, r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100), and n is the number of
monthly payments. At zero interest the result is principal ÷ n. The result is an estimate, not
a lender quote: fees, insurance, taxes, and changing rates are not included.

### Mortgage Calculator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/calculators/mortgage-calculator/

A mortgage payment is the fixed monthly amount of principal and interest that repays a home
loan in full over its term. This page is written for US readers and formats results in dollars
with US digit grouping. Inputs: loan amount, annual interest rate, and term in years or months.
Outputs: estimated monthly payment, total payment, and total interest. It uses the same
reducing-balance formula as the EMI Calculator; only the currency, grouping, and wording
differ. The estimate covers principal and interest only — property tax, homeowners insurance,
private mortgage insurance, closing costs, and adjustable-rate changes are not included.

### BMI Calculator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/calculators/bmi-calculator/

Body mass index (BMI) is a screening number calculated as weight in kilograms divided by
height in metres squared. Inputs: height and weight in metric (kg, cm) or imperial (lb,
feet/inches) units. Outputs: BMI value and screening category. BMI is a screening tool, not a
diagnosis; it does not distinguish muscle from fat, and it does not replace medical advice.
The page cites the World Health Organization's adult BMI categories (see Sources).

### CGPA to Percentage — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/calculators/cgpa-to-percentage/

CGPA to percentage conversion estimates a percentage from a 10-point Cumulative Grade Point
Average, commonly by multiplying the CGPA by 9.5 under the CBSE convention. Inputs: a CGPA
on the 10-point scale. Output: an estimated percentage. The result is labelled an estimate on
the page because no single conversion rule applies everywhere: many universities publish their
own formula, and the ×9.5 rule is a CBSE school-board convention. Always confirm against the
formula printed on your own marksheet or issued by your board or university.

### Word Counter — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/text/word-counter/

A word counter measures a piece of text by counting its words, characters, sentences, and
estimated reading time. Inputs: any pasted or typed text; counting updates as you type.
Outputs: word count, character count, sentence count, and estimated reading time. Everything
stays in the browser — text is never uploaded.

### Text to Speech — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/text/text-to-speech/

Text to speech converts written text into spoken audio using voices provided by the reader's
own browser. Inputs: typed or pasted text, plus a voice, rate, and pitch chosen from the voices
the browser makes available. Output: spoken audio played in the browser. There is no audio
download and no server processing: the tool uses the browser's built-in speech synthesis
(Web Speech API). Available voices depend on the visitor's browser and operating system, so
the same text can sound different on different devices.

### Fancy Text Generator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/text/fancy-text-generator/

A fancy text generator replaces ordinary Latin letters with visually styled Unicode characters
that can be copied and pasted. Inputs: plain text. Outputs: the same text rendered in 10
Unicode styles (bold, italic, script, monospace, and more), each with a copy button. The
styling is not a font: the characters themselves change to styled Unicode code points, mostly
from the Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols block (U+1D400–U+1D7FF) in the Unicode Standard.
Because the characters change, styled text may not match plain-text search, and screen readers
may announce code-point names rather than the visual style.

### Base64 Encoder/Decoder — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/dev/base64-encoder-decoder/

Base64 is a reversible encoding that represents binary data using letters, digits, plus,
slash, and padding. It is not encryption. Inputs: UTF-8 text to encode, or a Base64 string to
decode. Outputs: the encoded or decoded text, with a copy button. The encoding follows
IETF RFC 4648. Because Base64 is trivially reversible, it must never be used to hide
passwords, tokens, or other secrets.

### Invoice Generator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/tools/invoice-generator/

An invoice is a document a seller gives a buyer that lists goods or services, quantities,
prices, tax, and the total amount owed. Inputs: seller and buyer details, invoice number and
dates, item lines with quantity and unit price, tax, and notes. Currency: Indian rupee (INR)
or US dollar (USD), with digit grouping that follows the chosen currency. Outputs: a clean
invoice with subtotal, tax, and total, printable or savable as PDF from the browser. No
watermark is added. The page does not check tax rules — confirm what your jurisdiction
requires, such as a tax identification number.

### Fake Text Generator — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/fun/fake-text-generator/

A fake text generator creates a fictional chat mockup for sketches, presentations, and
entertainment. It is not connected to any messaging app. Inputs: fictional sender and receiver
names and made-up messages. Outputs: a chat-style mockup that can be exported as a PNG image.
The tool is for clearly fictional content; it must not be used to fabricate conversations and
present them as real.

## Guides

- How to Calculate EMI by Hand — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/guides/how-to-calculate-emi/
  Worked reducing-balance EMI examples with verified numbers.
- How to Calculate Your Age in Days — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/guides/how-to-calculate-age-in-days/
  Verified day counts, leap-year handling, and why dividing by 365.25 gives the wrong answer.
- CGPA to Percentage: The CBSE ×9.5 Rule, Explained — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/guides/cgpa-to-percentage-cbse-9-5-rule/
  What the ×9.5 rule means, where it applies, and where it does not.
- EMI Calculator vs Mortgage Calculator: Which One to Use — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/guides/emi-vs-mortgage-calculator/
  Same formula, different currency, formatting, and context — how to pick.
- All Guides — https://tulyrotools.vercel.app/guides/

## Sources cited on tool pages

- WHO — Obesity and overweight (adult BMI categories): https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/obesity-and-overweight
- IETF RFC 4648 — The Base16, Base32, and Base64 Data Encodings: https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc4648/
- MDN — SpeechSynthesis (Web Speech API): https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SpeechSynthesis
- The Unicode Standard — Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols (U+1D400–U+1D7FF): https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/Unicode-18.0/U180-1D400.pdf
- US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — How does paying down a mortgage work?: https://consumerfinance.gov:443/ask-cfpb/how-does-paying-down-a-mortgage-work-en-1943/

Tools without a Sources section have none because no genuine authoritative source applies to
them; sources are never invented.
